subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

There is only one way / to have a happier marred life / and I will learn it soon.

options.text: I and I will learn it soon.
to have a happier marred life

solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. to have a happier marred life .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in option 4: "to have a happier marred life."
 
• The word **"marred"** is incorrectly used in this context. "Marred" means damaged or spoiled and is not suitable when describing a happy life.
 
• The correct word should be **"married"**, as the sentence is likely referring to a "happier married life."

Correct sentence: *There is only one way to have a happier married life, and I will learn it soon.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Word Usage:** Be cautious about homophones (words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings) like "marred" and "married."
 
• Always check the context of the sentence to ensure the word choice makes sense.
